evidence: X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray reﬂectivity (XRR) measurements were used to determine ﬁlm density using a Bruker D8 X-ray diffractomer with CuK incident xray . Crystallinity was measured using powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Bruker D8 XRD system). Time-of-ﬂight elastic recoil detection analysis (ToF-ERDA) was used to discover the elemental compositions of ﬁlms. A 13.6 MeV 79Br7+ ion beam was used to measure the ﬁlm composition and the data was analysed with Potku analysis software. Further elemental analysis was performed with an Escalab 250XI (Thermo Fischer Scientiﬁc) microprobe was used for X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements. The surface roughness was estimated using atomic force microscopy (AFM)(Nanoscope IIIA microscope). The root-meansquared (RMS) roughness values were calculated using 2× 2 µm areas. The band gap of the NiO ﬁlms grown onto borosilicate glass (0.7 mm thick) were measured using ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis) (machine). Scanning electron microscopy was used to assess ﬁlm uniformity (JEOL JSM6301F FESEM) and the growth of NiO was conﬁrmed using X-ray analysis (Oxford INCA X-ray analyser).
